Incorporation of Companies.front: Minimum number of subscribers required to form an OPC, a private company and a public company at incorporation?
Incorporation of Companies.back: 1 OPC; 2 private company; 7 public company. (Minimum subscribers required to sign the Memorandum.)

Incorporation of Companies.front: Within how many days must a newly formed company notify its registered office and which form/section?
Incorporation of Companies.back: 30 days — file INC‑22 notifying registered office; s.12 Companies Act, 2013.

Incorporation of Companies.front: Declaration of commencement of business — who, when, which form?
Incorporation of Companies.back: Every company having a share capital: a director files INC-20A within 180 days of incorporation, confirming subscribers have paid for their shares (s.10A). Until then it cannot commence business or borrow.

Incorporation of Companies.front: What are the numeric thresholds that define a 'Small Company' under the Act?
Incorporation of Companies.back: Paid‑up capital ≤ ₹10 crore AND turnover ≤ ₹100 crore. (Definition: s.2(85).)

Incorporation of Companies.front: State the nationality and residency requirements for the member/nominee of an OPC, and any ceiling on capital/turnover.
Incorporation of Companies.back: Member/nominee must be a natural person, Indian citizen and resident (stayed in India ≥120 days). No capital or turnover ceiling for OPC.

Incorporation of Companies.front: Which clauses must the Memorandum of Association compulsorily contain at incorporation?
Incorporation of Companies.back: Name clause; registered office clause; object clause; liability clause — and capital clause if company has share capital. (Memorandum contents: s.4.)

Incorporation of Companies.front: Who signs/adopts the Articles on incorporation and what's their legal effect?
Incorporation of Companies.back: Subscribers sign and adopt the Articles; Articles form a contract between the company and its members. (Articles: s.5.)

Incorporation of Companies.front: Is any minimum paid‑up capital required to incorporate a company under the Companies Act, 2013?
Incorporation of Companies.back: None — there is no statutory minimum paid‑up capital required for incorporation under the Companies Act, 2013.

Incorporation of Companies.front: What declaration must accompany incorporation filings (Form INC‑9) and who must make it?
Incorporation of Companies.back: A declaration (INC‑9) by subscribers and first directors stating compliance with law and identity; filed at incorporation (can be certified by professional).

Incorporation of Companies.front: If a company has share capital, how many shares must each subscriber to the Memorandum take?
Incorporation of Companies.back: At least 1 share each — each subscriber must take and subscribe to the shares stated against their name in the Memorandum.

Incorporation of Companies.front: Doctrine of ultra vires — effect of an act beyond the objects clause?
Incorporation of Companies.back: Void ab initio; cannot be ratified even by all shareholders (Ashbury Railway Carriage v. Riche). The company is not bound, and directors may be personally liable.

Constructive notice: outsiders are deemed to know the MOA/AOA. Indoor management (Royal British Bank v. Turquand): they may assume internal procedure was followed. No protection for forgery, knowledge of irregularity, or suspicious circumstances.

Incorporation of Companies.front: Shifting the registered office — what approval is needed?
Incorporation of Companies.back: Within the same city/town: Board resolution. Outside local limits, same State: special resolution. One ROC to another in the same State: + Regional Director's confirmation. State to State: SR + Central Government (RD) approval, alter MOA.

Formed for charity, science, art, sport, education, etc.; profits applied to objects; NO dividend to members. Licence from the Central Government; need not use 'Limited'. Can never be a small company.

Incorporation of Companies.front: Alteration of articles and entrenchment (s.14, s.5)?
Incorporation of Companies.back: Articles altered by special resolution. Entrenchment makes specified provisions alterable only on stricter conditions — agreed by ALL members (private) or by special resolution (public).

Introduction — Preliminary Law.front: State the paid-up capital and turnover limits that qualify a company as a 'Small company' (section)?
Introduction — Preliminary Law.back: ₹10 crore paid‑up capital and ₹100 crore turnover; s.2(85). G.S.R. 880(E) effective 1‑Dec‑2025.

Introduction — Preliminary Law.front: Within how many days must a company notify its registered office after incorporation and which form is used?
Introduction — Preliminary Law.back: 30 days; s.12. File Form INC‑22 within 30 days of incorporation to furnish registered office particulars.

Introduction — Preliminary Law.front: By when must a company file the declaration of commencement of business (except where exempt) and which form/section governs it?
Introduction — Preliminary Law.back: 180 days; s.10A. File Form INC‑20A (declaration of commencement of business) within 180 days of incorporation.

Introduction — Preliminary Law.front: Give the member/nominee, nationality and residence requirements for a One Person Company (OPC).
Introduction — Preliminary Law.back: 1 person; member/nominee must be a natural person, Indian citizen and resident in India for ≥120 days; s.2(62) and Companies (Incorporation) Rules.

Introduction — Preliminary Law.front: What are the minimum numbers of members required for a public company, a private company and an OPC?
Introduction — Preliminary Law.back: 7 (public), 2 (private), 1 (OPC); see the definitions of public, private and OPC in s.2.

Introduction — Preliminary Law.front: What are the statutory minimum numbers of directors for a public company, a private company and an OPC? Cite the section.
List the mandatory clauses that must appear in the Memorandum of Association (name the number of clauses).
Introduction — Preliminary Law.back: 6 clauses: Name, Registered office (state), Objects, Liability, Capital, Subscription; s.4 (contents of memorandum).

Introduction — Preliminary Law.front: What is the maximum number of members permitted in a private company (section)?
Introduction — Preliminary Law.back: 200 members maximum; s.2(68) (definition of private company).

Introduction — Preliminary Law.front: How does the Act define 'company' (give the section and the exact frame of definition)?
Introduction — Preliminary Law.back: 1 definition: 'company' means a company incorporated under this Act or under any previous company law; s.2(20).

Introduction — Preliminary Law.front: State briefly the legal effect of Articles of Association and cite the section.
Introduction — Preliminary Law.back: 1 rule: Articles are the company’s internal regulations binding the company and its members; s.5.

Introduction — Preliminary Law.front: What is required of subscribers in the subscription clause of the Memorandum at incorporation?
Introduction — Preliminary Law.back: Each subscriber must take at least one share; subscription clause is part of memorandum (s.4) and subscribers must sign and state number of shares taken.

Subsidiary (s.2(87)): the other company controls the composition of its Board, or controls more than one-half of total voting power. Associate (s.2(6)): significant influence = at least 20% of voting power, but not a subsidiary.

Introduction — Preliminary Law.front: When can the corporate veil be lifted?
Introduction — Preliminary Law.back: Fraud or improper conduct, evasion of tax or law, the company being a sham or agent of its members, enemy character, and where statute provides. Starting point is separate personality — Salomon v. Salomon.

Introduction — Preliminary Law.front: Which companies can NEVER be a small company?
Introduction — Preliminary Law.back: A public company, a holding company, a subsidiary company, a section 8 company, and a company governed by a special Act — whatever their capital and turnover.

Prospectus and Allotment of Shares.front: Which section of the Companies Act defines 'prospectus' exam-correctly?
Prospectus and Allotment of Shares.back: Section 2(70): 'prospectus' = any document inviting offers from the public to subscribe for securities (includes red‑herring and shelf prospectuses).

Prospectus and Allotment of Shares.front: What is the validity period of a shelf prospectus and where is it authorised?
Prospectus and Allotment of Shares.back: 1 year — shelf prospectus permitted under Section 31; valid for one year from date of filing (Companies Act read with Prospectus & Allotment Rules).

Prospectus and Allotment of Shares.front: What crucial detail is omitted from a red‑herring prospectus (RHP)?
Prospectus and Allotment of Shares.back: Excludes price and quantum of securities — RHP contains all other disclosures but omits final price/number; used in book‑building until price fixed.

Prospectus and Allotment of Shares.front: What is the maximum number of persons to whom securities can be offered by private placement in a financial year?
Prospectus and Allotment of Shares.back: 200 persons — aggregate limit per financial year for private placement (Section 42); excludes qualified institutional buyers and employees.

Prospectus and Allotment of Shares.front: Private placement — time to allot, and if not allotted?
Prospectus and Allotment of Shares.back: Allot within 60 days of receiving application money; else refund within 15 days after that; else repay with interest at 12% p.a. Money must sit in a separate bank account (s.42(6)).

Prospectus and Allotment of Shares.front: If allotment is not made within 60 days, what is the refund timing and consequence for delay?
Prospectus and Allotment of Shares.back: 15 days — refund must be made within 15 days after the 60‑day period; if delayed, company pays interest (statutory rate widely applied as 12% p.a. for late refunds).

Prospectus and Allotment of Shares.front: Return of allotment in PAS-3 — time limits?
Prospectus and Allotment of Shares.back: Private placement: within 15 days of allotment (s.42(8)). Other allotments: within 30 days (s.39(4)).

Prospectus and Allotment of Shares.front: Misstatement in a prospectus — s.34 vs s.35 vs s.36?
Prospectus and Allotment of Shares.back: s.34: CRIMINAL liability (punishable as fraud u/s 447). s.35: CIVIL liability to compensate those who subscribed. s.36: punishment for fraudulently inducing persons to invest.

No allotment unless the minimum amount stated in the prospectus is subscribed. Application money at least 5% of nominal value (or as SEBI specifies). Not received within 30 days of issue → refund within 15 days of closure.

Prospectus and Allotment of Shares.front: Private placement — consequence of breaching s.42?
Prospectus and Allotment of Shares.back: Offer to more than 200 persons, or any advertisement, makes it a deemed PUBLIC offer. Penalty on company, promoters and directors: up to the amount raised or ₹2 crore, whichever is lower; refund within 30 days of the order.

Prospectus and Allotment of Shares.front: Shelf prospectus vs red herring prospectus?
Prospectus and Allotment of Shares.back: Shelf (s.31): valid 1 year for multiple issues; an information memorandum before each later issue. Red herring (s.32): lacks price/quantum; filed with ROC at least 3 days before the offer opens.

Shares and Debentures.front: Securities premium account — the only permitted uses (s.52)?
Shares and Debentures.back: Fully paid bonus shares; preliminary expenses; commission/discount/expenses on issue of securities; premium on redemption of preference shares or debentures; buyback u/s 68. Nothing else.

Offered to existing equity holders in proportion to paid-up capital; open 15 to 30 days; right of renunciation; not accepted = deemed declined. ESOP: special resolution. Preferential allotment: SR + registered valuer's price.
Special resolution, valid 12 months. Per year: 15% of paid-up equity or ₹5 CRORE in value, whichever is higher. Overall cap 25% of paid-up equity. Lock-in 3 years.

Shares and Debentures.front: State the statutory numerical limits and essential conditions for a company buyback of shares.
Shares and Debentures.back: 25% of aggregate of paid‑up capital and free reserves and ≤25% of paid‑up equity in a year; maintain ≤2:1 debt‑equity; board-only buyback ≤10%; one‑year gap between buybacks. (Section 68)

Shares and Debentures.front: Within what maximum period must redeemable preference shares be redeemed?
Shares and Debentures.back: Within 20 years from date of issue. (Section 55)
Out of free reserves, securities premium or CRR only — NEVER a revaluation reserve. Not in lieu of dividend. Once announced, cannot be withdrawn. Partly paid shares must first be made fully paid.

Shares and Debentures.front: When is appointment of a debenture trustee mandatory and where must the debenture trust deed/trustee particulars appear?
Shares and Debentures.back: Mandatory for a public issue of debentures; trustee and trust‑deed particulars must be disclosed in the prospectus and filed as required. (Section 71)

Shares and Debentures.front: By when must a company file the return of allotment (Form PAS‑3) with the Registrar of Companies?
Shares and Debentures.back: 30 days from the date of allotment — file Form PAS‑3 under Companies (Share Capital & Debentures) Rules.

Subscribers to MOA: 2 months from incorporation. Allotment: 2 months. Transfer/transmission: 1 month from receipt of the instrument. Debentures: 6 months from allotment. Transfer instrument lodged within 60 days of execution.
Equal to the NOMINAL value of shares bought back out of free reserves or securities premium. Usable only to issue fully paid bonus shares.
Reduction: special resolution + confirmation by the Tribunal (NCLT). Buyback: no Tribunal — board resolution up to 10%, special resolution up to 25%.

Acceptance of Deposits by Companies.back: ss.73 to 76A with the Companies (Acceptance of Deposits) Rules, 2014. s.73: prohibition + deposits from members. s.76: eligible public companies from the public. s.76A: punishment.

Acceptance of Deposits by Companies.front: Deposit limits — who can take how much?
Acceptance of Deposits by Companies.back: Eligible public company: 10% of capital + free reserves + securities premium from members, 25% from public. Government eligible company: 35% from public. Other public company: 35% from members. Private company: 100% from members.

Acceptance of Deposits by Companies.front: Interest on deposits not repaid on maturity?
Acceptance of Deposits by Companies.back: Penal interest at 18% p.a. for the overdue period (Rule 17).

Acceptance of Deposits by Companies.front: Return of deposits — form and due date?
Acceptance of Deposits by Companies.back: Form DPT-3, on or before 30 June every year, with information as on 31 March, duly audited.
On or before 30 April each year, deposit at least 20% of deposits maturing during the FOLLOWING financial year in a scheduled bank. Usable only for repaying deposits.

Acceptance of Deposits by Companies.front: Who is outside Chapter V altogether?
Acceptance of Deposits by Companies.back: Banking companies, NBFCs registered with RBI, housing finance companies registered with NHB, and other companies the Central Government specifies.

Acceptance of Deposits by Companies.front: What mandatory corporate action must a public company take before accepting deposits from persons other than its members?
Acceptance of Deposits by Companies.back: Special resolution + prescribed circular: public company must pass a special resolution and circulate the prescribed offer/circular (Form DPT‑1) before accepting deposits from non‑members (Rules).
A PUBLIC company with net worth of at least ₹100 crore OR turnover of at least ₹500 crore, which has obtained prior consent by special resolution filed with the ROC, and a credit rating every year.
Not less than 6 months and not more than 36 months. Exception: up to 10% of capital + free reserves for 3 to 6 months to meet short-term needs. No deposits repayable on demand.

Acceptance of Deposits by Companies.front: Amounts that are NOT deposits (Rule 2(1)(c)) — the common ones?
Acceptance of Deposits by Companies.back: From Government/banks/financial institutions; from another company; share application money allotted within 60 days; from a DIRECTOR out of his own funds (with declaration); secured debentures; advances for goods/services adjusted within 365 days.
Company: fine of at least ₹1 crore or twice the deposit (whichever lower), up to ₹10 crore. Officer in default: imprisonment up to 7 years and fine ₹25 lakh to ₹2 crore; fraud u/s 447 if wilful.

Registration of Charge.front: Within how many days must a company register a charge with the Registrar after its creation?
Registration of Charge.back: 30 days — deliver particulars to Registrar within 30 days of creation; failing registration renders the charge void against the liquidator and creditors (but valid inter se).

Registration of Charge.front: What is the legal effect of non‑registration of a company’s charge?
Registration of Charge.back: Void against liquidator and creditors; remains valid between company and charge‑holder; no enforceable priority against third parties until registered.

Registration of Charge.front: Which date determines priority of a charge against other creditors — date of creation or date of registration?
Registration of Charge.back: Date of registration — priority against third parties and in liquidation is determined by the date of registration, not the date of creation.

Registration of Charge.front: How long after full satisfaction must a company file particulars of satisfaction of a charge with the Registrar?
Registration of Charge.back: 30 days — file particulars of satisfaction with the Registrar within 30 days of full satisfaction, attaching the instrument/certificate as required.

Registration of Charge.front: Which types of charges must be registered to be effective against third parties?
Registration of Charge.back: Any charge on company assets or undertaking — fixed, floating, mortgage, hypothecation, etc.; registration required to be effective against creditors and liquidator.

Registration of Charge.front: Does a floating charge require a fresh registration when it crystallises?
Registration of Charge.back: No — crystallisation of a floating charge does not require fresh registration; the original registered charge governs priority and enforceability.

Registration of Charge.front: What statutory records must a company keep at its registered office about charges?
Registration of Charge.back: A register of charges with particulars (date, amount, creditor, property, instrument reference) and copies of charge instruments; open for inspection on payment of prescribed fee.

Registration of Charge.front: Missed the 30 days — what are the extended windows (s.77)?
Registration of Charge.back: Up to 60 days from creation: ROC may allow with additional fees. A further 60 days (120 in all): with ad valorem fees. Beyond that: only the Central Government can extend, u/s 87.

Registration of Charge.front: Company does not register the charge — what can the lender do (s.78)?
Registration of Charge.back: The charge-holder may himself apply after the 30 days. ROC gives the company 14 days' notice; then registers. He recovers the fees paid from the company.

Registration of Charge.front: Satisfaction of charge (s.82) — time and form?
Registration of Charge.back: Intimate the ROC within 30 days of payment in full, Form CHG-4; ROC may allow up to 300 days with additional fees. ROC issues a memorandum of satisfaction.

Registration of Charge.front: Effect of registration on third parties (s.80)?
Registration of Charge.back: Any person acquiring the charged property is DEEMED to have notice of the charge from the date of its registration.

Management and Administration.front: Annual return (s.92) — form, due date, certification?
Management and Administration.back: MGT-7 (MGT-7A for OPC and small companies) within 60 days of the AGM. Certified in MGT-8 by a CS in practice if listed, or paid-up capital ₹10 crore+ or turnover ₹50 crore+.

First AGM: within 9 months of the close of the first FY (no ROC extension). Later: within 6 months of FY close; gap not over 15 months. ROC may extend by 3 months. 9 AM to 6 PM, not a national holiday.

Members holding 1/10th of paid-up voting capital. Board must move within 21 days and hold it within 45 days of the requisition; else requisitionists hold it within 3 months. Expenses recovered from defaulting directors.
Need not be a member; cannot speak; votes only on a poll. One person: proxy for max 50 members and 10% of voting capital. Deposit 48 hours before; inspection from 24 hours before.

Management and Administration.front: Poll demand vs special notice — the fractions?
Management and Administration.back: Poll (s.109): 1/10th of total voting power OR ₹5 lakh paid-up capital. Special notice (s.115): 1% of voting power OR ₹5 lakh paid-up capital. Same ₹5 lakh, different fractions.
At least 7 days' prior notice. Closed for not more than 30 days at a stretch and 45 days in a year.

Holds, alone or together, beneficial interest of at least 10% in shares, voting rights or distributable dividend, or exercises control/significant influence. BEN-1 to the company; company files BEN-2.
MGT-14 within 30 days of passing — all special resolutions and specified Board resolutions and agreements.

Management and Administration.front: How many days’ notice is required for a general meeting and how can shorter notice be validly given?
Management and Administration.back: 21 days & 95% — general meeting notice at least 21 days; shorter notice valid only with consent of members holding at least 95% of voting power (s.101).
Public company: 5 members if up to 1,000 members; 15 if 1,001 to 5,000; 30 if more than 5,000. Private company: 2. PERSONALLY present — proxies do not count; a s.113 corporate representative does.

Management and Administration.front: Within what time must minutes of meetings be signed and by whom?
Management and Administration.back: 30 days — minutes of board and general meetings to be signed by the chairperson of the meeting (or of the next meeting) within 30 days (s.118).

Management and Administration.front: No quorum within half an hour — what happens?
Management and Administration.back: Meeting stands adjourned to the same day next week, same time and place. If it was called on REQUISITION, it stands cancelled. At the adjourned meeting, members present are the quorum.
Ordinary: votes for exceed votes against. Special: intention stated in the notice, and votes for are at least THREE TIMES the votes against.

Management and Administration.front: Report on AGM (s.121) and postal ballot (s.110)?
Management and Administration.back: AGM report: listed public companies only, MGT-15 within 30 days. Postal ballot: mandatory for notified items; not required for OPC and companies with up to 200 members.

Audit and Auditors.front: Within how many days must a company file the auditor’s appointment with the Registrar (Form ADT‑1)?
Audit and Auditors.back: 15 days — file Form ADT‑1 with the Registrar after appointment of auditor. (Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules; s.139 context.)

Audit and Auditors.front: Within how many days must a resigning auditor file his statement of resignation with the Registrar (Form ADT‑3)?
Audit and Auditors.back: 30 days — auditor files Form ADT‑3 with the Registrar giving reasons for resignation. (Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules; s.140 context.)

Audit and Auditors.front: What are the maximum continuous terms for an individual auditor and for an audit firm (rotation rule)?
Audit and Auditors.back: Individual: 5 consecutive years; Firm: 10 consecutive years (two terms of 5). Cooling‑off period after expiry: 5 years. (Section 139(2) — rotation provisions.)

Audit and Auditors.front: Casual vacancy in the office of auditor (s.139(8))?
Audit and Auditors.back: Board fills it within 30 days. If caused by RESIGNATION, the appointment must also be approved by the company in general meeting within 3 months of the Board's recommendation. Holds office till the next AGM.

Audit and Auditors.front: What statutory rights does an auditor have to obtain information and inspect company records?
Audit and Auditors.back: Unrestricted access to books, vouchers and records; right to require information/explanations and attendance of officers. (Section 143(1).)

Audit and Auditors.front: State the key matters an auditor must report on under Section 143(3).
Audit and Auditors.back: Whether F/S give true & fair view and comply with accounting standards; proper books maintained; adequacy and operating effectiveness of internal financial controls. (Section 143(3).)

₹1 crore or more: report to Board/Audit Committee within 2 days, seek reply within 45 days, then forward to the Central Government within 15 days (ADT-4). Below ₹1 crore: to Board/Audit Committee only; disclosed in Board's report.

Audit and Auditors.front: Tenure of an auditor appointed at an AGM (s.139(1))?
Audit and Auditors.back: From the conclusion of that AGM till the conclusion of the SIXTH AGM — a five-year term. Annual ratification by members is no longer required.

Audit and Auditors.front: What must the principal auditor do when a branch is audited by a branch auditor?
Audit and Auditors.back: Disclose in the main audit report reliance on the branch auditor’s work, consider the branch auditor’s findings and state that branch was separately audited. (Section 143(8).)
Appointed by the Board within 30 days of incorporation; failing which, by members at an EGM within 90 days. Holds office till the conclusion of the FIRST AGM.
Listed companies; unlisted PUBLIC companies with paid-up capital ₹10 crore+; PRIVATE companies with paid-up capital ₹50 crore+; any company with public borrowings/deposits of ₹50 crore+.

Self/relative/partner holding securities (a RELATIVE may hold up to ₹1 lakh face value); indebted above ₹5 lakh; guarantee above ₹1 lakh; business relationship. Also: officer/employee, body corporate (LLP allowed), more than 20 audits.

Audit and Auditors.front: Removing an auditor before his term (s.140(1))?
Audit and Auditors.back: Board resolution → application to the Central Government in ADT-2 within 30 days → on approval, special resolution within 60 days. Auditor must get a reasonable opportunity of being heard.
Accounting and book-keeping; internal audit; design of financial information systems; actuarial; investment advisory; investment banking; outsourced financial services; management services.

File ADT-3 within 30 days of resignation with the company and the ROC (also with the CAG for government companies), stating reasons. Default: penalty of ₹50,000 or audit fees, whichever is less, plus ₹500 a day.

Declaration of Dividends.front: From what source may a company declare dividend? Quote the limit and section.
Declaration of Dividends.back: Only out of profits of the company for that year or previous years (after providing depreciation); not out of capital except as permitted — Section 123(1).

Declaration of Dividends.front: When is a company barred from declaring dividend on equity shares (s.123(6))?
Declaration of Dividends.back: While it is in default of sections 73 and 74 — acceptance and repayment of DEPOSITS. (Do not confuse with s.70, which bars BUYBACK for deposit, debenture, preference and term-loan defaults.)

Declaration of Dividends.front: Who can declare an interim dividend and under which section?
Declaration of Dividends.back: The Board of Directors may declare an interim dividend during a financial year — Section 123(3).

Declaration of Dividends.front: Time to pay a declared dividend, and the punishment (s.127)?
Declaration of Dividends.back: Within 30 days of declaration. Default: every director knowingly a party — imprisonment up to 2 years and fine of at least ₹1,000 a day; company pays simple interest at 18% p.a.

Declaration of Dividends.front: If declared dividend remains unpaid after 30 days, what must the company do and by when? Give the section.
Declaration of Dividends.back: Transfer unpaid/unclaimed dividend to a separate Unpaid Dividend Account in a scheduled bank within 7 days of expiry of the 30‑day payment period — Section 124(1).

Declaration of Dividends.front: After how long must unpaid/unclaimed dividend be transferred to the Investor Education and Protection Fund (IEPF) and by when must the transfer be completed?
Declaration of Dividends.back: 7 years — unpaid/unclaimed dividend not paid/claimed for seven consecutive years must be transferred to IEPF; transfer to be made within 30 days of the completion of seven years — Section 124(5).

Declaration of Dividends.front: Who is entitled to receive a dividend when a company declares it — give the precise determining date and section.
Declaration of Dividends.back: The person registered as the member on the date of declaration is entitled to the dividend — right vests on the record date (date of declaration) — Section 126.

Declaration of Dividends.front: If shares are transferred after the date of declaration but before payment, who gets the dividend? Cite the section.
Declaration of Dividends.back: The registered holder on the date of declaration gets the dividend; a transfer after the declaration does not entitle the transferee — Section 126 (classic examiner trap).

Declaration of Dividends.front: In what form may dividend be paid (s.123(5))?
Declaration of Dividends.back: Only in CASH — cheque, warrant or electronic mode — to the registered holder or his banker. Capitalising profits to issue fully paid bonus shares is not barred by this rule.

Declaration of Dividends.front: If a dividend already transferred to IEPF is claimed later by the shareholder, where and how is the refund claim made?
Declaration of Dividends.back: The shareholder/nominee can claim refund from the IEPF Authority under the prescribed procedure; IEPF rules provide for refund of such amounts to entitled persons — Section 125 (IEPF refund mechanism).

Declaration of Dividends.front: Dividend out of accumulated reserves when profits are inadequate — the conditions?
Declaration of Dividends.back: Rate not above the average of the 3 preceding years; withdrawal not above 1/10th of paid-up capital + free reserves; amount first used to set off the year's losses; reserves after withdrawal at least 15% of paid-up capital.

Declaration of Dividends.front: Interim dividend when the company has a loss in the current year?
Declaration of Dividends.back: Rate cannot exceed the average of dividends declared in the 3 immediately preceding financial years (s.123(3)). It caps the rate; it does not bar the dividend.

Declaration of Dividends.front: Unpaid Dividend Account — statement and interest (s.124)?
Declaration of Dividends.back: Statement of names and unpaid amounts on the company's website within 90 days of the transfer. Default in transferring: interest at 12% p.a. for the members' benefit.

Declaration of Dividends.front: What goes to the IEPF after 7 years?
Declaration of Dividends.back: The unpaid/unclaimed dividend AND the underlying SHARES on which dividend has been unclaimed for 7 consecutive years (s.124(5), (6)). Both can be reclaimed from the IEPF Authority.

Accounts of Companies.front: Where must a company keep its books of account and for how long must they be preserved?
Accounts of Companies.back: 8 years — Books of account to be kept at registered office (or at other place as Board authorises) and preserved for 8 financial years (Section 128).

Accounts of Companies.front: What is the statutory test for company financial statements and which sections mandate accounting‑standard compliance?
Accounts of Companies.back: True & fair view — Financial statements must give a true and fair view and comply with accounting standards notified under Section 133 (requirement in Section 129; see s.133 for AS power).

Accounts of Companies.front: Which companies need not prepare a cash flow statement (s.2(40))?
Accounts of Companies.back: One Person Company, small company (paid-up up to ₹10 crore AND turnover up to ₹100 crore), dormant company, and a private company that is a start-up.

Accounts of Companies.front: When must a company prepare consolidated financial statements and which AS govern them?
Accounts of Companies.back: Holding with subsidiary/associate/joint venture — Holding company must prepare consolidated financial statements per AS 21/23/27, as required under Section 129(3).

Accounts of Companies.front: Who must sign the company’s financial statements before circulation or AGM?
Accounts of Companies.back: At least two directors — Financial statements must be approved by the Board and signed on behalf of the Board by at least two directors (one MD if any); CEO/CFO/Company Secretary must sign if appointed (Section 134).

Accounts of Companies.front: What must the Directors’ Responsibility Statement in the Board’s Report contain?
Accounts of Companies.back: Statutory confirmation — Board’s Report must include a Directors’ Responsibility Statement confirming true & fair view, accounting standards compliance and adequacy of internal controls (Section 134).

Accounts of Companies.front: What is a member’s statutory right to obtain company financial statements?
Accounts of Companies.back: Free copy — Any member or debenture‑holder entitled under Section 136 can obtain a copy of the audited financial statements, auditor’s and Board’s reports; company must furnish copies (Section 136).

Accounts of Companies.front: Within what time must financial statements, auditor’s report and Board’s report be filed with the Registrar?
Accounts of Companies.back: 30 days — File financial statements, auditor’s report and Board’s report with the Registrar within 30 days of the AGM (Section 137).

Accounts of Companies.front: Which e‑form is used to file annual financial statements with the ROC and what is the deadline?
Accounts of Companies.back: AOC‑4 — Audited financial statements are filed with the ROC in e‑form AOC‑4 within 30 days of the AGM; consolidated FS (if any) filed in AOC‑4 CFS as applicable (Section 137 and Rules).

Accounts of Companies.front: CSR (s.135) — when does it apply and how much?
Accounts of Companies.back: Any ONE in the immediately preceding FY: net worth ₹500 crore+, turnover ₹1,000 crore+, or net profit ₹5 crore+. Spend 2% of average net profits of the 3 preceding FYs. No CSR Committee if the obligation is ₹50 lakh or less.
130: only on a court/Tribunal order, for fraud or mismanagement; up to 8 years back. 131: directors' own application with Tribunal approval; any of the 3 preceding FYs; once a year.

Accounts of Companies.front: Internal audit (s.138) — unlisted public company thresholds?
Accounts of Companies.back: Paid-up capital ₹50 crore+, or turnover ₹200 crore+, or bank/PFI borrowings above ₹100 crore, or deposits ₹25 crore+. Private company: turnover ₹200 crore+ or borrowings above ₹100 crore. Every listed company.

Accounts of Companies.front: Filing financial statements — OPC, and if not adopted at the AGM?
Accounts of Companies.back: Normally AOC-4 within 30 days of the AGM. OPC: within 180 days of the close of the FY. If not adopted, file unadopted statements within 30 days; ROC takes them as provisional.

Companies Incorporated outside India.front: Give the statutory definition of a 'foreign company' that makes Chapter XXII provisions applicable.
Companies Incorporated outside India.back: A company incorporated outside India which has a place of business in India (by itself, through an agent, physically or electronically) or conducts any business activity in India — i.e., a foreign company with an Indian place of business.

Companies Incorporated outside India.front: Within how many days must a foreign company furnish documents to the Registrar after opening a place of business in India?
Companies Incorporated outside India.back: 30 days — deliver required particulars and documents to the Registrar from the date of opening any place of business in India.

Companies Incorporated outside India.front: Name the core documents a foreign company must deliver to the Registrar on registration (five essentials).
Companies Incorporated outside India.back: Five: certified copy of its charter/constitutional documents, list of directors with addresses, particulars of principal place(s) of business in India, name/address of person authorised for service in India, English translations where necessary.

Companies Incorporated outside India.front: Within what period must changes in directors, principal Indian office or authorised agent be notified to the Registrar?
Companies Incorporated outside India.back: 30 days — intimate the Registrar of any change in directors, change of principal place(s) of business in India, or change of authorised person for service, within 30 days of the change.

Companies Incorporated outside India.front: Who should be appointed as agent for service of process in India and what happens if none is appointed?
Companies Incorporated outside India.back: One person resident in India must be appointed and his address filed with the Registrar; if none is appointed, service of process may be effected through the Registrar on the company’s behalf.

Companies Incorporated outside India.front: Where must a foreign company keep statutory books and financial records relating to its Indian business?
Companies Incorporated outside India.back: At its principal place of business in India (the registered Indian office) — books, accounts and records must be maintained there and made available for inspection as required.

Companies Incorporated outside India.front: Which annual documents must a foreign company file in respect of its Indian place of business?
Companies Incorporated outside India.back: Copies of its balance-sheet, profit & loss account, auditors’ report and list of directors/managers concerned with the Indian operations — filed annually in the prescribed form and manner.

Companies Incorporated outside India.front: Foreign company fails to comply with Chapter XXII — effect on its contracts (s.393)?
Companies Incorporated outside India.back: Contracts stay VALID and it can be sued — but the company cannot bring any suit, claim a set-off or counter-claim on them until it complies.

Companies Incorporated outside India.front: When must a foreign company comply as if it were an Indian company (s.379(2))?
Companies Incorporated outside India.back: Where not less than 50% of its paid-up share capital is held by Indian citizens and/or companies or bodies corporate incorporated in India.

Companies Incorporated outside India.front: Accounts of a foreign company (s.381) — filing time?
Companies Incorporated outside India.back: Balance sheet, P&L and a list of all places of business in India, within 6 months of the close of the financial year; ROC may extend by up to 3 months.

Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008.front: Minimum partners and designated partners; who is 'resident'?
Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008.back: At least 2 partners; at least 2 designated partners who are individuals, one of them resident in India — i.e. stayed in India at least 120 days during the financial year (s.7).

Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008.front: Is there a maximum limit on number of partners in an LLP?
Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008.back: No maximum — unlimited number of partners permitted; partners governed by LLP agreement (no statutory cap).

Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008.front: State the statutory due-dates for the two annual LLP filings and their calendar equivalents.
Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008.back: Form 11 (Annual Return): within 60 days of FY-end (by 30 May). Form 8 (Statement of Accounts & Solvency): within 30 days from end of six months after FY-end (by 30 October).

Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008.front: When is an LLP required to get its accounts audited? Give the numeric thresholds.
Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008.back: Audit mandatory if turnover in a financial year exceeds ₹40 lakh OR contribution (capital) exceeds ₹25 lakh in that year.

Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008.front: Describe the extent of partners' liability in an LLP (numeric/qualitative rule).
Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008.back: Liability limited to the agreed contribution; partners are not personally liable for LLP debts except for their own wrongful acts, fraud or as provided in the LLP agreement.

Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008.front: What happens to LLP’s existence when partners change? (succession rule)
Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008.back: Perpetual succession — LLP is a separate legal entity; changes in partners/designated partners do not affect the LLP’s existence or continuity.

Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008.front: Within what time must change in partners or designated partners be intimated to the Registrar?
Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008.back: 30 days — any appointment, cessation or change in partners/designated partners must be filed with the Registrar within 30 days of the change.

Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008.front: State the rules on capital contribution — minimum amount, form, and recording requirement.
Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008.back: No statutory minimum contribution; can be cash, kind or service as agreed. Contribution particulars must be recorded in the LLP agreement and Statement of Account (annual filing).

Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008.front: Can a partnership firm or a private company convert into an LLP? Give the basic condition(s).
Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008.back: Yes — conversion permitted by filing prescribed documents and executing an LLP agreement; conversion requires compliance with creditor protections and statutory filing requirements.

Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008.front: Who bears primary legal responsibility for statutory compliance of the LLP (designation/role)?
Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008.back: Designated partners — they are responsible for regulatory filings and compliance; failure can attract personal liability and penalties for designated partners.

Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008.front: Whose agent is a partner of an LLP (s.26)?
Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008.back: Agent of the LLP — NOT of the other partners. The LLP is liable for his wrongful acts in the course of business; other partners are not personally liable.

Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008.front: When is liability UNLIMITED in an LLP (s.30)?
Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008.back: Where the LLP or its partners act with intent to defraud creditors or for a fraudulent purpose: unlimited for the LLP and for the partners who acted so. Also imprisonment up to 5 years and fine ₹50,000 to ₹5 lakh.

Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008.front: No LLP agreement, or it is silent — what governs (s.23(4))?
Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008.back: The First Schedule: equal share in capital and profits, every partner may take part in management, no remuneration for management, new partner only with consent of all.

Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008.front: Fewer than 2 partners for more than 6 months?
Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008.back: The sole partner who carries on business knowing this is PERSONALLY liable for obligations incurred in that period (s.6). It is also a ground for winding up.

General Clauses Act, 1897.front: How long is a 'month' under the General Clauses Act for statutory time computation?
General Clauses Act, 1897.back: 1 calendar month; 'month' means calendar month (definition) — count by calendar months, not fixed number of days.

General Clauses Act, 1897.front: Who does the word 'person' include when used in a statute?
General Clauses Act, 1897.back: Includes every company, association or body of persons, natural or artificial — whether incorporated or not (general definition rule).

General Clauses Act, 1897.front: How must singular/plural and masculine/feminine words be read in statutory language?
General Clauses Act, 1897.back: Singular includes plural and vice‑versa; masculine includes feminine — words import the other gender/number unless context forbids.
'From' EXCLUDES the first day; 'to' INCLUDES the last day.

General Clauses Act, 1897.front: Last day falls on a day the court or office is closed (s.10)?
General Clauses Act, 1897.back: The act is in time if done on the NEXT day on which the court or office is open. It saves only the last day — it is not a general extension.

General Clauses Act, 1897.front: What is the legal effect of repeal of an enactment on acts done before repeal?
General Clauses Act, 1897.back: Repeal does not affect previous acts, rights, liabilities or penalties incurred before repeal — saved unless express contrary provision.
Deemed effected by properly addressing, pre-paying and posting by registered post — at the time the letter would be delivered in the ordinary course, unless the contrary is proved.

General Clauses Act, 1897.front: Does the General Clauses Act treat 'writing' to include printed material?
General Clauses Act, 1897.back: Yes — 'writing' includes printing, lithography and other modes of representing words in visible form (inclusive definition).

General Clauses Act, 1897.front: How are references to a government department/office treated if its name or organisation changes?
General Clauses Act, 1897.back: Reference applies to the successor authority or new name — reorganisation or renaming does not defeat statutory reference unless contrary intent.

General Clauses Act, 1897.front: When does a Central Act come into operation if no date is stated (s.5)?
General Clauses Act, 1897.back: On the day it receives the President's assent. It operates from the first moment of that day (s.5(3)).

Unless a different intention appears: previous operation of the law, rights and liabilities accrued, penalties incurred, and pending proceedings all survive. Repeal does not revive anything not in force.

General Clauses Act, 1897.front: Power to appoint (s.16) and power to make rules (s.21)?
General Clauses Act, 1897.back: s.16: power to appoint includes power to suspend or dismiss. s.21: power to issue notifications, orders, rules or bye-laws includes power to add to, amend, vary or rescind them.

General Clauses Act, 1897.front: Key definitions in s.3 — 'financial year', 'good faith', 'immovable property'?
General Clauses Act, 1897.back: Financial year: commencing on 1 April. Good faith: done honestly, whether negligently or not. Immovable property: includes land, benefits arising out of land, and things attached to the earth.

Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999.front: 'Person resident in India' u/s 2(v) — the test and its exceptions?
Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999.back: Resided in India more than 182 days in the PRECEDING financial year — BUT not one who has gone or stays abroad for employment, business or an uncertain period. A person coming to India for those purposes becomes resident. Purpose beats day-count.

Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999.front: Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) limit and who can use it?
Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999.back: USD 250,000 per financial year — available to every resident individual (including minors via guardian) for education, travel, medical, gifts, investments and purchase of foreign assets (RBI LRS rules).

Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999.front: Which authorities administer and regulate foreign exchange under FEMA?
Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999.back: 2 authorities — Central Government frames rules; Reserve Bank of India regulates/authorises persons, issues directions and implements FEMA/forex policy (RBI is the operational regulator).

Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999.front: Short checklist: what is a 'current account transaction' under FEMA?
Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999.back: Payments for goods, services, short‑term remittances, interest, dividends, maintenance — current account covers flow of income and consumptive transactions (distinguished from capital account transactions).

Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999.front: Short checklist: what is a 'capital account transaction' under FEMA?
Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999.back: Transactions altering assets/liabilities (acquisition/transfer of immovable property abroad/India, investments, loans, guarantees) — capital account changes financial position, not routine payments.

Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999.front: Who may legally deal in foreign exchange or foreign securities?
Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999.back: Only RBI‑authorised persons — banks and entities authorised by RBI (Authorised Dealers/Money‑chang ers/Authorised Persons) can buy/sell foreign exchange or deal in foreign securities.
Up to THRICE the sum involved where quantifiable; otherwise up to ₹2 lakh. Continuing contravention: up to ₹5,000 for every day after the first. Civil, adjudicated by the Adjudicating Authority.
On application, by the RBI or Directorate of Enforcement, within 180 days of the application. Once compounded, no further proceedings for that contravention.

Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999.front: Export/import of Indian currency — what is permitted?
Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999.back: Prohibited except with RBI permission — export or import of Indian currency notes/coins requires RBI authorisation; rules govern permitted foreign currency carriage (RBI/Customs rules apply).

Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999.front: How is foreign investment (FDI) routed under FEMA/FDI policy?
Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999.back: 2 routes — Automatic Route (no prior government approval) and Government Route (prior approval required); sectoral caps/conditions are governed by FEMA regulations and FDI policy notifications.

Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999.front: Current vs capital account — the rule of freedom?
Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999.back: Current account (s.5): FREE, subject to reasonable restrictions by the Central Government. Capital account (s.6): permitted only to the extent RBI/Central Government allow. Free unless restricted vs restricted unless permitted.

Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999.front: Current account transactions — Schedules I, II and III?
Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999.back: Schedule I: PROHIBITED (remittance of lottery winnings, racing income, purchase of lottery tickets, banned magazines). Schedule II: prior approval of the Central Government. Schedule III: RBI approval beyond specified limits; individuals — LRS USD 2,50,000.

Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999.front: Realisation and repatriation of export proceeds (s.7, s.8)?
Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999.back: Exporters must furnish a declaration of full export value and realise and repatriate the proceeds to India within the period RBI specifies. Residents must take reasonable steps to bring back foreign exchange due.

Interpretation of Statutes.front: Which interpretative rule is applied first and requires words be given their ordinary meaning?
Interpretation of Statutes.back: 1. Literal (grammatical) rule — give words their plain, ordinary meaning; applied first; do not import extraneous intent beyond the text.

Interpretation of Statutes.front: When is the golden rule used and what does it permit the court to do?
Interpretation of Statutes.back: 2. Golden rule — modify literal meaning to avoid absurdity or repugnance; used only if literal meaning produces absurd or impossible result.

Interpretation of Statutes.front: What four questions form the mischief rule (Heydon's case) test?
Interpretation of Statutes.back: 3. Mischief rule (Heydon) — ask: (i) common law before Act, (ii) defect/mischief, (iii) remedy Parliament intended, (iv) true reason; interpret to suppress mischief.

Interpretation of Statutes.front: When is the purposive approach employed instead of strict literalism?
Interpretation of Statutes.back: 4. Purposive rule — ascertain legislative purpose and interpret contextually; used for ambiguous provisions or modern social/economic statutes to effect legislative intent.

Interpretation of Statutes.front: How does ejusdem generis limit general words that follow specific words?
Interpretation of Statutes.back: 5. Ejusdem generis — general words following specifics are limited to the same kind/quality as the specific items.

Interpretation of Statutes.front: What does expressio unius exclusio alterius mean and when is it applied?
Interpretation of Statutes.back: 6. Expressio unius — naming one or more things implies exclusion of others; used only where the statutory scheme suggests an exhaustive list.

Interpretation of Statutes.front: How does noscitur a sociis help interpret a lone word in a list?
Interpretation of Statutes.back: 7. Noscitur a sociis — a word gets meaning from its surrounding words; prevents isolated, out-of-context interpretations.

Interpretation of Statutes.front: Name three presumptions courts apply when interpreting statutes (retrospectivity, constitutionality, penal/tax).
Interpretation of Statutes.back: 8. Presumptions: (i) statutes not retrospective unless clearly stated; (ii) constitutionality presumed; (iii) penal/tax statutes construed strictly against state.

Interpretation of Statutes.front: How must a proviso or a non obstante clause be treated when reading a statute?
Interpretation of Statutes.back: 9. Proviso/non obstante — proviso qualifies the main enactment; non obstante overrides inconsistent laws; read together; proviso cannot expand the enacting provision beyond intent.

Interpretation of Statutes.front: What test decides whether a statutory provision is mandatory or directory?
Interpretation of Statutes.back: 10. Mandatory vs directory — examine language, purpose and consequences; if breach voids object/result, it's mandatory; if merely procedural with no fatal consequence, directory.

Interpretation of Statutes.front: Give three internal aids and three external aids used in statutory interpretation.
Interpretation of Statutes.back: 11. Internal/external aids — internal: long title, preamble, definitions; external: legislative history/reports, prior statutes, authoritative dictionaries.

Interpretation of Statutes.front: What does in pari materia mean and when do you apply it?
Interpretation of Statutes.back: 12. In pari materia — statutes on the same subject are read together for harmonious construction; avoid conflict; later or specific enactment may prevail.

Interpretation of Statutes.front: What is the practical order courts follow among literal, golden, mischief and purposive rules?
Interpretation of Statutes.back: 13. Order of approach — apply literal rule first; if absurd, apply golden; if still unclear, apply mischief (Heydon) and purposive/contextual rules; stop when meaning is settled.
